comparison.approach: four semantic test shards plus a dedicated syntax-check job
comparison.correctness: high; every prior npm-test file remains covered
comparison.robustness: high; failures isolate to queue-core, worker-reliability, distributed-faults, or synthetic-sandboxes
comparison.latency: lower critical path through bounded parallelism
comparison.resourceUse: moderate and bounded to five jobs
comparison.regressionRisk: low; production code is untouched and fail-fast is disabled so all subsystem results are collected
comparison.qa: same test inventory, explicit syntax gate, semantic fault localization

whyItWon: It preserves complete coverage while turning an opaque aggregate failure into actionable subsystem evidence. The bounded parallelism improves time-to-diagnosis without the runner cost and maintenance burden of one job per file.
failuresAndLessons: A green monolithic suite is sufficient for release confidence, but a red monolithic suite is poor operational telemetry when job logs are unavailable through the connected interface.
CI observability is part of reliability engineering: diagnostic resolution determines how quickly regressions in distributed worker semantics can be isolated safely.
Syntax checking should remain independent from behavioral tests so parser/import regressions do not obscure runtime fault-test outcomes.
The shard boundaries must stay semantic and must be updated whenever new test files are added to package.json.
nextGate: use the first sharded run to identify the failing subsystem, repair the root cause with a regression test, then require all shards green before Qubes worker testing
